3. SEO in your CMS

Discover SEO implementation across various CMS platforms with our comprehensive collection of expert-backed guides and actionable resources. Whether you’re working with WordPress, Shopify, Wix, Magento, Webflow, or Squarespace, implementing effective SEO strategies in your content management system is crucial for organic growth.

Each CMS handles SEO differently—from URL structures and metadata management to technical configurations and plugin ecosystems. That’s why we’ve curated the most reliable, up-to-date SEO resources tailored specifically for each platform. You’ll discover step-by-step tutorials, best practices, and proven optimization techniques that help you leverage your CMS’s full SEO potential.

From beginners looking to learn SEO online to experienced marketers seeking advanced CMS-specific strategies, these free SEO resources cover everything you need: technical setup, content optimization, site architecture, and performance improvements. Explore platform-specific guidelines below to transform your CMS into an SEO powerhouse and drive meaningful organic traffic to your website.

Tips when Executing SEO in your CMS

Implementing SEO successfully in your CMS requires understanding both platform-specific nuances and universal best practices. These insights from seasoned SEO professionals highlight critical considerations, common pitfalls to avoid, and strategic approaches that work across different content management systems.

“WP: Pay close attention to what you want crawled and indexed, and send clear signals on those pages. For example, rarely if ever do you want tag pages indexed. Tools like Yoast & Rank Math can help you control indexation through meta robots, canonicals, etc. Be careful not to accidentally “introduce” new page and asset types you don’t want indexed to Google – by including them on XML sitemaps. This happens – frequently! – when you set up new SEO plugins and forget to configure the default settings. Big picture, never forget that these wonderful plugins are really “tools”. Tools you can use wisely… or accidentally harm yours site. A tool is not a strategy. Rather, pick the right tool for the job, and leverage it correctly to help implement your game plan! Also: make sure to select a solid redirect plugin, like Simple 301 Redirects or Redirection (double-check that it works with your hosting provider- they don’t all.) Having the ability to implement simple pattern matching or regex-formatted redirects is a huge win!”
Tory Lynne Gray
X Linkedin Threads
“Regardless of which CMS you use, I think it’s worth it for any SEO to make sure they understand how the CMS structures content and thus what URLs they create. For example, with WordPress, users may not realize that their implementation is creating separate URLs for authors, month & years post archives, and media attachments. On Shopify, you may end up having multiple versions of one product page because of all the Collection versions as well. This can eat up crawl budget and water down your share of unique content.”
Sam Torres
X Linkedin Threads
“Read the documentation. Every CMS has very lengthy documentation that talks about how it works, why it works, and so on. More often than not, they have some very specific SEO considerations. You want to understand how they handle metadata. You want to make sure that you have the capability to edit page titles, meta descriptions, structured data, and all types of other metadata. You want to make sure that it allows you to do 301 redirects. There is always going to be a use case for changing where a piece of content lives. And then internal links. You need to have the capability to add internal links between pages. In some cases, the CMS doesn’t allow you to add HTML. They are only WYSIWYG environments. Not sure why that exists or why that’s a thing. But you need to know that the CMS has the capability. “
Mike King
X Linkedin Threads
“For WordPress, it’s critical to interrogate all of your settings. A good SEO plugin will take care of the back-end, sure! But then you need to assess every single public URL you have. Similar tags? Consolidate them. Attachment pages? Redirect them. Thin archives? Populate them! If you want to go deeper, you need to interrogate *everything* your site’s doing – beyond just your SEO settings! Plugins slowing you down? Replace them! Comment spam? Protect against it! Links broken? Monitor them! SEO plugins provide tools, but you still need to think + manage.”
Jono Alderson
X Linkedin Threads
“Create templates for your team to use that are set up for SEO success. Making SEO easy to use/implement increases the odds that your team will give a damn about SEO. Bonus points if you also create documentation explaining how and when to use said templates.”
Tess Voecks
X Linkedin Threads
“- Define your web architecture before choosing your CMS. The topic and the main keyword / keywords you are going to work on each page.

– On a WP / wocommerce before creating the products and categories, define and write the permalinks for your online store based on your strategy.

-If you are starting an e-commerce with WP, define the categories and subcategories from the beginning, and which product goes in each one. Keep in mind how to organize the products that are in more than one or if you don’t want this to happen. “
Gemma Fontané

Sometimes adapting templates and changing page layouts of finished theme can itself cause a lot of technical SEO problems with loading, crawling or indexing. Define what modules and SEO widgets do you need based on the website architecture, type of the website and issues you want to avoid. Research best rated modules and test first before you apply it site-wide, to make sure it works with your template and does not cause any issues.”

SEO for CMS FAQs

Many of the most popular content management systems (CMS) in the market, such as WordPress, Wix or Shopify provide SEO functionalities, whether natively or through free plugins, to facilitate fundamental SEO related configuration, like optimizing titles, meta descriptions, headings, meta robots, canonical tags, redirects, robots.txt, and more. It’s recommended to validate first to ensure the Web platform you’re considering using will give you those configurations that are a must for your own context. It’s also important to take into account, that although a CMS can facilitate to execute SEO configurations, they’re not a replacement of an SEO specialist. To see positive results, it’s a must knowing how to configure those functionalities and align any execution with a relevant SEO strategy, connected to your Website business and marketing goals. 

Yes, a CMS can help SEO by providing tools and features that make it easier to optimize your website. Most modern CMS platforms offer built-in SEO settings, plugins, and user-friendly interfaces for managing metadata, URLs, sitemaps, and more, streamlining the optimization process for users of all skill levels.

CMS SEO is the ability of your Website content management system to implement SEO-related configurations through features or functionalities that minimize the time and/or need for Web development support. 

Most modern CMS platforms offer user-friendly SEO features and plugins that don’t require coding knowledge. Start with basic optimizations like customizing page titles, meta descriptions, and URLs. Install recommended SEO plugins (like Yoast for WordPress or built-in tools for Shopify), which guide you through essential configurations. Focus on creating quality content, using proper heading structures, and following the platform-specific guides listed above for step-by-step instructions.

Common SEO mistakes in a CMS include leaving default URLs unchanged, ignoring meta descriptions, creating duplicate content across pages, neglecting image optimization, and failing to submit XML sitemaps. Many users also overlook mobile responsiveness, page speed optimization, and proper redirect management when updating or deleting content. Each CMS has unique challenges—for instance, Wix users might struggle with URL customization, while WordPress users may install conflicting SEO plugins.

Yes, but careful planning is essential for a successful CMS migration. Before migrating, assess if the new Web platform will allow you to effectively configure the key SEO related configurations and offer the possibility to create a crawlable and indexable Web structure with a crawlable navigation, descriptive URLs, and avoid any over-reliance on Client Side Render JS, among other key configurations.

If you decide to go ahead with the migration, document all URLs, meta data, and content. Set up 301 redirects from old URLs to new relevant ones, maintain the same content structure where possible, and submit updated XML sitemaps to search engines. Monitor your rankings closely during and after migration, and be prepared for temporary fluctuations. Consider hiring an SEO professional for complex migrations to minimize ranking losses.
